info.title: Mnemic API — contract foundation
info.description: Partial contract for health, feature flag management, project-scoped belief APIs, conversation lifecycle/read and Provider/configuration APIs (Issue #24). Other implemented API families and the online documentation page are not included yet. Error type URIs are stable identifiers, not guaranteed live web pages.

put.summary: Replace all feature flags with revision checking
put.description: JSON-only full replacement, no query parameters. Audit and update are atomic; unchanged flags do not increase revision or write an audit. Unsupported true flags (retrieval_entity, retrieval_time, decay, reranker, read_time_resolution) return 400 before database access even though their syntactic type is boolean. Cache-Control: no-store.

get.summary: List project beliefs with filters and offset pagination
get.description: Operator scope, not per-user ownership. Unknown query keys are ignored. Default status active, server limit 200 (max 1000), offset 0. q is literal case-insensitive subject/attribute containment, not value search. Missing projects return an empty list. Order is subject then attribute; offset pages are not a stable snapshot during concurrent changes. No model calls.

post.summary: Correct a belief with user-correction authority
post.description: Synchronous standard ingest/resolver path with USER_CORRECTION provenance. Deleted beliefs must be explicitly restored first (409); retracted beliefs may be revived. Body requires a nonempty string; unknown keys are stripped, whitespace is not trimmed. Query keys ignored. No extraction or embedding model call. This does not provide write-side secret detection; do not submit credentials as corrections.

get.summary: List project conversations with message counts
get.description: Global operator scope, not user-level ownership. Default limit 200 (max 1000), offset 0. Unknown query keys ignored. Missing project yields []. Stable order started_at then id, but offset pages are not a snapshot under concurrent writes. Counts include verified inherited messages. Broken/missing/foreign inherited references preserve the row with message_count=null and history_error=unavailable; otherwise count is an integer and history_error absent. This coupling is a runtime refinement. No model calls.

get.summary: Read complete message timeline and resolved memory citations
get.description: Includes inherited message references, without copying them. Full unpaginated history ordered by msg_time then id. Citations resolve against the same project, including historical/deleted beliefs; foreign or missing citation IDs are omitted. memories=null differs from a present empty array. Optional file metadata does not copy attachment content; raw_text is the stored message. Attachment parent/path constraints are validated at runtime; corrupt history or file parents return409. Query ignored. No model calls.

post.summary: Archive a conversation and register pending Evidence extraction
post.description: Legacy global-ID route: project ownership is inferred from the conversation, no project parameter. Same global Bearer operator authorization applies. UUID is validated by the shared generation guard before database access. No required body; query ignored. Repeated commits, busy generation or invalid context return409. extraction_triggered means work registered, never extraction/indexing completed. With pending physical user/file Evidence, formal entry durably enqueues it in the archive transaction; library builds without a queue retain asynchronous in-process jobs. These jobs may invoke models and consume quota; this endpoint is not a paid probe.

post.summary: Create a new conversation referencing verified source history
post.description: Always creates a new fork, returns201, and archives open source/current conversations; never reopens or copies messages. Source and optional current_conversation_id must both belong to the URL project. An explicit JSON object (including {}) is required; unknown body keys rejected, query ignored. Reserved manual-corrections conversations and corrupt history return409. File paths/parents are validated at runtime. Any pending physical Evidence may be queued/extracted as for commit; inherited history is not extracted again. No automatic retry after an uncertain response.

post.summary: Create encrypted Provider configuration with one or more model slots
post.description: Requires DB and master key. Body extras are stripped, including unknown models keys. Strings are not trimmed; old generic URL validator remains (unlike PATCH). At least one nonempty chat/extraction/embedding model is required by runtime refinement. Key encryption, config creation and metadata-only audit share a transaction. Does not contact the endpoint, validate embedding dimensions or invoke any model. Duplicate name409. Do not submit a real credential to the offline example.

patch.summary: Patch existing Provider metadata and chat/extraction models
patch.description: Requires DB; never decrypts key or constructs SDK. Strict body and models reject unknown fields, api_key and embedding. At least one field and nonempty models patch required by runtime refinements. Supplied strings are trimmed; URL must be HTTP(S) without credentials/query/fragment and trailing slashes are normalized. A Provider carrying an embedding slot cannot change endpoint/protocol (409); re-embedding is not implemented here. Unchanged patches return current config without audit; actual change and metadata-only audit are atomic. Successful handler responses are no-store. Query ignored.

get.summary: Read safe Provider and selected model slot snapshot
get.description: DB required, master key not required. No query parameters accepted. No key decryption, SDK construction or model calls; no key/mask in response. Safe HTTP(S) endpoints strip username/password/query/fragment; other URLs become null. Invalid metadata rows are omitted from providers and their IDs reported; an invalid earliest candidate yields model=null/invalid=true, not silent fallback. Selection order created_at then id, as SDK resolution. At most1000 providers; overflow500. This snapshot is not a connectivity/readiness proof. Handler responses no-store.
